steps.en: What you see: The left ventricle is a thick walled circle with two papillary muscles, anterolateral and posteromedial, jutting into the cavity like short fingers. The walls should thicken toward the centre with every beat.
Landmarks to confirm: Do not accept the view until each of these is on screen.
Common mistakes and how to correct them: Each mistake below comes from the view catalogue with its correction.
Normal values: Septal and posterior wall thickness at end diastole: 6 to 10 mm in men, 6 to 9 mm in women.
Measure at end diastole with the leading edge to leading edge method.
Left ventricular ejection fraction 55 percent or more is normal.

Pitfalls: Including a papillary muscle in the wall measurement overstates thickness and fakes hypertrophy. Compare thickening in every wall, since a wall that stays still while the rest move points to ischaemia in that territory.

analogy.en: Landmarks to confirm: Cavity of left ventricle

spot.en: Landmarks to confirm: Cavity of left ventricle
Lateral papillary muscle of left ventricle
Anterolateral head of lateral papillary muscle
Common mistakes and how to correct them: Oblique cut that makes one papillary muscle vanish. Correct it by rocking the probe until both muscles appear together and the cavity is round.
Including mitral chordae by sitting too basal. Correct it by sweeping toward the apex until chordae give way to solid muscle heads.
Apical cut where the cavity looks small and hypertrophied. Correct it by sweeping toward the base until the cavity opens to its widest circle.

todo.en: How to get it: Place the probe at left sternal edge, fourth intercostal space, mid sweep.
Point the probe marker toward the left shoulder, about two o clock.
This is the level for thickness measurement. Freeze at end diastole, at the start of the QRS, and measure the septum and posterior wall without including the papillary muscles.
Freeze the image only when every listed landmark is on screen at once.

remember.en: Measure wall thickness at end diastole.

q.en: When do you freeze to measure wall thickness?

o.en: End diastole at the start of the QRS

why.en: Thickness is an end diastolic measurement, timed to the start of the QRS.

q.en: The septum measures 14 mm with the muscle head included. What do you do?

o.en: Reposition the calliper clear of the papillary muscle

why.en: Muscle heads must stay outside the calliper, so remeasure wall only.

q.en: One wall fails to thicken while the rest move well. What does this suggest?

why.en: Regional failure of thickening points to ischaemia in that wall.
